html:
The Defenestration of Prague of 23 May 1618 was the throwing of two Catholic governors and their secretary from a high window of Prague Castle by angry Protestant nobles, an act that started the Thirty Years' War.

The nobles accused the officials of breaking the Letter of Majesty, which had promised Bohemian Protestants religious freedom. All three survived the fall of some 20 metres, landing on a dung heap according to Protestants and saved by angels according to Catholics. The Bohemian estates rose against the Habsburgs and chose the Protestant Frederick V of the Palatinate as king. The revolt was crushed at the White Mountain in 1620, but the war spread across Europe. An earlier defenestration in 1419 had started the Hussite Wars.
sum: The Defenestration of Prague of 23 May 1618 was the throwing of two Catholic governors and their secretary from a high window of Prague Castle by angry Protestant nobles, an act that started the Thirty Years' War.
